messages.subject: Re: 3D polygons in R
parts:
Dear Daniel,

Thanks for your message. For working with 3D meshes, the tools I use are

* Rvcg R package
* Morpho R package
* meshlab app

I normally use wavefront OBJ format as my interchange format. You can
use the readobj package to import big meshes. Rvcg has the option to
write OBJ meshes (don't use the rgl version – see thread with Dudi
Deutsch for details).

For making meshes from volumetric data, I normally uses Amira. However
you can use Fiji. There is a marching cubes implementation in the 3D
viewer plugin if you make a binary mask of your data. You can then save
to Wavefront OBJ, STL etc. You can follow the first part of the "3D
Content in PDFs" from https://imagej.net/3D_Viewer:_Screencasts. You can
also script this like so: https://imagej.net/3D_Viewer:_Display_a_Stack

To plot surface meshes in R, I either use rgl (e.g. wire3d or mesh3d) or
wrappers of these functions in nat (essentially plot3d.* methods).
Recently we have provided some support in nat using plotly. The pros and
cons of rgl vs plotly are discussed here:

http://natverse.org/nat/articles/plotly.html

Hope this helps. With best wishes,

Greg.

PS I have taken the liberty of ccing this message to the nat-user google
group since the answer may be of interest to others.
